predecessors.name: Mahan confederacy
predecessors.text: Wiryeseong, where 'Onjo settled ... and called his country Shipje'; Paekche 'initially belonged to the Mahan confederacy'

successors.name: Tang dynasty
successors.text: the Baekje area, for which the 'Tang government set up Ungjin Commandery for the purpose of governing the Paekche area' (Baekje page)

successors.name: Silla
successors.text: most of the former Baekje, taken from the Tang from 671; Baekje 'ultimately submitted to Unified Silla'

ledger.x: 18 BCE: Onjo founds Baekje at Wiryeseong.
132: King Gaeru is believed to have moved the capital north of the river to Bukhansanseong.
From 234, Baekje spreads over Gyeonggi and Chungcheong.
369: Geunchogo annexes the last of Mahan.
371: Geunchogo moves the capital to Mt.
392: Gwanggaeto takes ten Baekje walled cities.
392-396: the war for the Han River heartland.
395: Baekje is pushed back to Wiryeseong ('was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong on the Han River').
396: Gwanggaeto captures the Baekje capital and Asin 'submitted to him', surrendering 'a prince and 10 government ministers'; the Han valley stays Baekje's until 475.
475: Goguryeo takes Wiryeseong.
475: the capital moves to Ungjin (Gongju): 'Paekche's capital was located at Ungjin' 475 to 538; infobox 476.
476: Tamna becomes Baekje's tributary.
538: King Seong moves the capital to Sabi.
After 538 the state calls itself Nambuyeo (Southern Buyeo).
551: Baekje retakes its old capital.
551: Baekje and Silla 'entered into an alliance to attack Goguryeo'; the Han River valley is fought over until 553.
553: Silla takes the Han River valley.
553: the Han River valley is Silla's.
660: the Baekje tributary relation ends with the fall of Baekje (infobox 'Tributary state of Baekje (498–660)').
660: Silla and Tang end Baekje.

wars.name: Baekje–Goguryeo war of 369-371
wars.outcome: Baekje repelled Goguryeo at Chiyang in 369; in 371 its army of 30,000 'took the fortress of Pyongyang and killed Gogugwon of Goguryeo'.

wars.name: Gwanggaeto's conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Goguryeo took ten walled cities in 392 and more land in 395; in 396 it captured the capital and Asin submitted.

wars.name: Goguryeo's conquest of Hanseong
wars.outcome: Jangsu captured Wiryeseong and killed King Gaero; Baekje moved to Ungjin.

wars.name: Baekje–Silla campaign against Goguryeo
wars.outcome: Baekje regained its old capital in 551; in 553 Silla took the Han River valley; King Seong was killed at Gwansanseong in 554.

wars.name: Silla–Tang conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Kim Yu-sin's Silla army won at Hwangsanbeol on 9 July 660 and, with Su Dingfang's Tang army, took the Baekje capital; King Uija surrendered and went into exile in China.

wars.name: Baekje restoration and Baekgang
wars.outcome: Dochim and Buyeo Boksin brought Buyeo Pung back from Japan with 10,000 soldiers; the Silla–Tang forces won the naval battles at Baekgang in August 663 and Pung escaped to Goguryeo.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is recorded.
